title: Continuous theta burst stimulation delays L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia progression and ameliorates orolingual dyskinesia with concomitant reduction of striatal FosB/DeltaFosB and neuroinflammation.
authors: Wu, Xiang; Sun, Qingfeng; Yang, Shuo; Wang, Yixuan; Bai, Yihua; Hui, Yanping; Li, Libo; Qiao, Hongfei; Zhang, Qiaojun; Wang, Ling
one_liner_zh: 该文研究连续θ爆发刺激对左旋多巴诱导运动障碍的缓解作用及纹状体FosB/神经炎症变化，属神经调控与疾病模型研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Chronic L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA) administration in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) inevitably leads to L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia (LID), which can be more disabling than PD itself. Therefore, finding ways to prevent or delay LID progression is crucial. Continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS), a patterned form of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, shows promise to alleviate LID. However, whether it can prevent or delay LID progression and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. In this study, we administered L-DOPA daily with or without concurrent cTBS to hemiparkinsonian rats for 3 weeks. Electromagnetic simulation confirmed that the dorsolateral striatum is within the electromagnetic field generated by cTBS. Prolonged L-DOPA administration deteriorated LID progressively, whereas cTBS significantly delayed the development of axial, limb, and total dyskinesia, with orolingual dyskinesia even improving over time. Additionally, L-DOPA administration significantly increased the number of FosB/DeltaFosB(+) cells and CD68(+)/Iba1(+) cells, with elevated iNOS, IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, and IL-6 levels, without altering total microglial numbers in the dorsolateral striatum. cTBS reversed all these changes, reducing FosB/DeltaFosB(+) cells, CD68(+)/Iba1(+) cells, and all 4 pro-inflammatory markers. Furthermore, FosB/DeltaFosB(+) cell numbers and pro-inflammatory marker levels positively correlated with the severity of total, axial, limb, and orolingual dyskinesia. Collectively, cTBS treatment delays the progression of LID and improves orolingual dyskinesia, which is closely associated with the reduction of FosB/∆FosB(+) cells and alleviation of microglia-related inflammation in the striatum.
abstract_zh: 帕金森病（Parkinson's disease, PD）患者长期服用L-3,4-二羟基苯丙氨酸（L-DOPA）不可避免地会导致L-DOPA诱导的运动障碍（LID），其致残程度可能超过PD本身。因此，寻找预防或延缓LID进展的方法至关重要。连续θ爆发刺激（continuous theta burst stimulation, cTBS）作为一种模式化的重复经颅磁刺激形式，显示出缓解LID的潜力。然而，它是否能预防或延缓LID进展及其潜在机制仍 largely 未知。在本研究中，我们对偏侧帕金森病大鼠连续3周每日给予L-DOPA，并联合或不联合cTBS治疗。电磁模拟证实，背外侧纹状体位于cTBS产生的电磁场范围内。长期L-DOPA给药使LID进行性恶化，而cTBS显著延缓了轴向、肢体和总运动障碍的发展，口舌运动障碍甚至随时间改善。此外，L-DOPA给药显著增加了FosB/DeltaFosB(+)细胞和CD68(+)/Iba1(+)细胞的数量，并升高了iNOS、IL-1β、TNF-α和IL-6水平，但未改变背外侧纹状体中总小胶质细胞数量。cTBS逆转了所有这些变化，减少了FosB/DeltaFosB(+)细胞、CD68(+)/Iba1(+)细胞及所有4种促炎标志物。进一步地，FosB/DeltaFosB(+)细胞数量和促炎标志物水平与总、轴向、肢体和口舌运动障碍的严重程度呈正相关。综上，cTBS治疗延缓了LID的进展并改善了口舌运动障碍，这与纹状体中FosB/∆FosB(+)细胞的减少及小胶质细胞相关炎症的缓解密切相关。
